title: The Ring of Fire
logline: At a night procession, a fire performer whirls a torch and the crowd sees a ring of fire. Up close there is only one flame, a pair of hands, and years of practice.
human_question: How much of what we see is really there, and how much is made by speed, distance and our own seeing?

premise.story: A fire performer's night, from rehearsal and preparation to the procession and after, told through the performer's own practice and risks.
premise.place: A night procession (perahera) with fire performers.
premise.experience: Drums, heat, darkness and circles of light, then the single flame and the tired hands that made them.

concept_links.why: The Margaya's own image of a concept: the ring of fire that exists only because a single flame moves fast [C001-M:L42].
Mind as a stream of extremely brief moments that feels like one continuous mind: the ring of fire turned inward.
What is actually there: heat, light and motion, not 'a ring'.

what_camera_could_observe: Wide shots: unbroken rings and figures of fire
Close and high-frame-rate shots: one flame on a stick
The performer's hands, wicks, fuel, preparation and burns
The crowd's faces lit by rings that do not exist
what_must_be_real: The performer's real practice, pay, risk and pride. Nothing is performed only for the camera.

possible_arc.opening: Darkness, drums, a ring of fire appears.
possible_arc.turn: The camera comes close and the ring becomes one flame, then one person.
possible_arc.ending_open: After the procession: embers, and whatever the performer really says about what the crowd saw.

position_hint: opening candidate: the most cinematic way to open the question of what is really there; an Object 1 acquisition would be possible only if it really happens

requirements: A procession with fire performers during the filming window

suggestions.name: Kandy Esala Perahera
suggestions.why: The best-known night procession, with fire performers among the dancers and drummers.
suggestions.access_notes: Very crowded; filming positions need organiser permission
suggestions.verify: Performer access and filming permissions are unverified.

suggestions.name: A village or regional perahera
suggestions.why: A smaller procession allows closer access to one performer's whole night.
suggestions.verify: A specific procession and performer must be found.

risks: Spectacle footage with no person at the centre
Religious ceremony must be treated with respect
drop_if: No performer will let the camera into their preparation and their night

connections.note: Both show a whole that seems solid but is made of moments (a ring, a morning).

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
